metadata.description: Phonetic pronunciation guides for all supported languages
metadata.note: Phonetics use simplified English-readable syllables with stress marks (CAPS = stressed syllable)

spanish.name: Español
spanish.phonetic_note: Stress on CAPS syllables. 'rr' = rolled r, 'ñ' = ny sound

french.name: Français
french.phonetic_note: Nasal vowels: 'an/en' = nasalized ah, 'on' = nasalized oh, 'in' = nasalized eh

german.name: Deutsch
german.phonetic_note: 'ch' = throat clearing sound, 'ü' = ee with rounded lips, 'ö' = eh with rounded lips

italian.name: Italiano
italian.phonetic_note: Double consonants are pronounced longer. 'gli' = lyee, 'gn' = ny

portuguese.name: Português
portuguese.phonetic_note: 'ão' = nasalized ow, 'nh' = ny sound, 'lh' = ly sound

russian.name: Русский
russian.phonetic_note: Stress is crucial - unstressed 'o' sounds like 'ah'

chinese.name: 中文
chinese.phonetic_note: Tones are critical. Numbers indicate tone: 1=flat, 2=rising, 3=dip, 4=falling

japanese.name: 日本語
japanese.phonetic_note: Vowels: a=ah, i=ee, u=oo, e=eh, o=oh. Double vowels held longer

korean.name: 한국어
korean.phonetic_note: Vowels similar to Spanish. 'eu' = uh sound

arabic.name: العربية
arabic.phonetic_note: Read right-to-left. 'kh' = throat sound, 'gh' = gargling sound, ''' = glottal stop

hebrew.name: עברית
hebrew.phonetic_note: Read right-to-left. 'ch' = throat sound like German 'ch'

amharic.name: አማርኛ
amharic.phonetic_note: Ge'ez script is syllabic - each symbol = consonant + vowel. Ejectives: k', t', ch' are 'popping' sounds

tigrinya.name: ትግርኛ
tigrinya.phonetic_note: Similar to Amharic. Uses Ge'ez syllabary

hindi.name: हिन्दी
hindi.phonetic_note: Aspirated consonants: 'kh', 'gh', 'th', 'dh' have a breath after. Retroflex: tongue curled back

bengali.name: বাংলা
bengali.phonetic_note: Similar to Hindi with regional variations

tamil.name: தமிழ்
tamil.phonetic_note: Retroflex sounds common. 'zh' = unique Tamil sound (tongue curled back)

telugu.name: తెలుగు
telugu.phonetic_note: Aspirated and retroflex consonants. Similar to other South Indian languages

thai.name: ไทย
thai.phonetic_note: 5 tones: mid, low, falling, high, rising. Tone marks crucial

vietnamese.name: Tiếng Việt
vietnamese.phonetic_note: 6 tones. Diacritics indicate tone and vowel quality

turkish.name: Türkçe
turkish.phonetic_note: 'ı' = uh sound, 'ö' = German ö, 'ü' = German ü, 'ş' = sh, 'ç' = ch

farsi.name: فارسی
farsi.phonetic_note: Read right-to-left. 'kh' = throat sound, 'gh' = French r sound

kurdish.name: Kurdî
kurdish.phonetic_note: Similar to Farsi with regional variations

swahili.name: Kiswahili
swahili.phonetic_note: Stress usually on second-to-last syllable. 'ng' = as in 'singer'

dutch.name: Nederlands
dutch.phonetic_note: 'g' = throat clearing sound, 'ij' = long i sound, 'oe' = oo sound

swedish.name: Svenska
swedish.phonetic_note: 'å' = oh sound, 'ä' = eh sound, 'ö' = German ö

polish.name: Polski
polish.phonetic_note: 'sz' = sh, 'cz' = ch, 'rz/ż' = zh, 'ą' = nasalized o, 'ę' = nasalized e

czech.name: Čeština
czech.phonetic_note: 'ř' = unique Czech sound (rzh), 'č' = ch, 'š' = sh, 'ž' = zh

hungarian.name: Magyar
hungarian.phonetic_note: 'gy' = dy, 'ny' = ny, 'sz' = s, 's' = sh, 'cs' = ch, 'zs' = zh
